newsitem.title: USA: Why probe White House database, Democrat asks.
newsitem.headline: Why probe White House database, Democrat asks.

text.p: The ranking Democrat on a congressional panel investigating the White House database Sunday questioned the panel's threat to subpoena information on personal events held at the White House.

Representative Collin Peterson, D-Minnesota, in a letter to the chairman of the subcommittee, defended the White House's response to the panel's investigation, and he had concluded there was no evidence that the White House database contained sensitive information.
Representative David McIntosh, R-Indiana, chairman of the House Subcommittee on National Economic Growth, Natural Resources and Regulatory Affairs, has been investigating the White House database.
McIntosh began his probe after reports in the Washington Times suggested the White House database may contain sensitive security information on individuals collected from government agencies.
The White House says the database is a system for managing the Clintons' contacts with friends, relatives, acquaintances and supporters.

Peterson said McIntosh had also threatened to subpoena information on President Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton's private, personal events at the White House, including a private dinner for their daughter Chelsea's school friends.
"I simply see no possible public policy or oversight concern that justifies the subcommittee threatening a subpoena," Peterson wrote in the letter.

He noted that the White House had agreed to allow any member of the subcommittee to see all information contained in the database, but did not want to release information on these personal events to congressional staff or any other outside party.

Peterson in the letter questioned McIntosh on the "purpose of this investigation," asking what wrongdoing he was suggesting had occurred and why he felt the need to subpoena information on personal events.
